newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay shares hit 3-year low, index falls two pct.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shares hit 3-year low, index falls two pct.

text.p: Bombay shares took a beating in nervous trade on Tuesday as the benchmark 30-share index tumbled to a new three-year low, traders said.
The Bombay Stock Exchange's (BSE) top index crashed 55.43 points, or 1.9 percent, to end at a provisional 2,796.0, just above the intra-day low of 2,795.41.
"There is a total absence of buyers in the market. It looks very bad ..." said Kamal Kabra, former president of the BSE.
"Shares are down on low volumes. People are slowly leaving the market." The two percent fall on Tuesday erased the market's previous three-year low of 2,811.17 on November 19, 1993.
Traders said an onslaught of bad news in recent weeks made investors jittery, with some selling pressure seen coming up in smaller stocks across-the-board.
"Small investors are also selling. We are seeing a falling market with no buying support at any level," said chief dealer Ketan Jhaveri at local brokerage Kotak Securities.
Participants said poor six-month results announced by top firms took their toll on market sentiment, with major players taking a bearish look at the market.
They said selling by local funds coupled with hammering of blue-chip stocks by foreign institutions pulled prices lower.
"I don't see any likely revival...the future looks bleak," said Kotak's Jhaveri.
India was the weakest performer in the Morgan Stanley Capital International (MSCI) index for emerging markets during November, an MSCI statement said on Tuesday.
India (-8.9 percent), Chile (-6.3 percent) and South Africa (-5.6 percent) figured among the poor performing emerging markets.
ACC fell 36.50 rupees to 930.0, Gujarat Ambuja Cement 11.70 to 191.0, Siemens 38.50 to 347.50, Bajaj Auto 36.70 to 756.25, M&M 9.25 to 266.25, SBI 7.25 to 209.25 and Dr Reddy's 16.75 to 152.25.
